name: Ernest Hemingway
hook: Nobel laureate, war novelist, Key West fixture — Jeopardy's Hemingway checklist.

facts.label: the Nobel Prize
facts.statement: Hemingway won the 1954 Nobel Prize in Literature but could not accept it in person after injuries from two plane crashes in Africa.

facts.label: The Sun Also Rises
facts.statement: The Sun Also Rises is his first novel; it opens "Robert Cohn was once middleweight boxing champion of Princeton" and echoes Gertrude Stein's "lost generation".

facts.label: A Farewell to Arms
facts.statement: A Farewell to Arms follows an American ambulance driver and the English nurse Catherine Barkley on the Italian front in World War I.

facts.label: For Whom the Bell Tolls
facts.statement: For Whom the Bell Tolls (1940) is about Robert Jordan in the Spanish Civil War; its title comes from a John Donne work.

facts.label: The Old Man and the Sea
facts.statement: The Old Man and the Sea (1952) won the Pulitzer; at the end Manolin agrees to fish with Santiago again.

facts.label: Key West
facts.statement: His home on Whitehead Street in Key West is famous for descendants of his six-toed cats and an annual Hemingway Days look-alike contest.

facts.label: A Moveable Feast
facts.statement: A Moveable Feast is his memoir of 1920s Paris, including pre-lunch whiskies and Perrier with F. Scott Fitzgerald.
